SR10 (2002) and SR11 (2023) restrict the operands to the file's RECORD KEY or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY in the same words, and 2002 already has record-key-name SOURCE (2002 8.4.5.1.3, file control). A key lives in the file's own record, so no CD reach is possible. The 2002 Format 1 random-read route (GR16: no NEXT/PREVIOUS means format 2 rules apply) has its twin in 2023. The 'dynamic access' definition changes only in wording. Sampled the reader's evidence: l1_read_key_of_reference gives MATCH at 2002 (log-2002.txt), and read-splitkey.cob at 2002 gives 'R 00 ABV1' then 'N 10'. That discriminates: in K1K2 order the NEXT would have returned BAV2. 2023's SUPPRESS WHEN on alternate keys is a widening.

cases.reason: Same formats. The rule governs the implied record of a record-less FD, sized by the RECORD clause. I compared the RECORD clauses: 2002 13.16.41 has formats 1-3 in CHARACTERS, sized in bytes (GR1); 2023 adds the synonym BYTES (SR2), a widening, with the same size rules. A record-less FD is a file FD in both editions, never a CD. The receiver identifier-1 is GR4's business. The 'alphanumeric group item' change concerns only variable-length groups (2014+). The witness pb345_record_less_fd_area_2023 gives MATCH at 2002 (log sampled).

cases.reason: The RELEASE formats and the sentence are identical, and EC-FLOW-RELEASE is 'Fatal | RELEASE not in range of SORT' in both tables. I attacked the deferral: 'set to exist' hands off to fatal-exception processing, and that changed in two ways. (1) 2002 14.5.12.1.1 counts EXIT FUNCTION and EXIT METHOD as ending a declarative abnormally; 2023 drops both statements. (2) 2023 adds step 2 of 14.6.13.1.3 (an executed MERGE or SORT follows its own rules), along with the PERFORM WHEN and APPLY COMMIT steps, none of which a 2002 program can reach. I probed the 2002-only route: rel-func-exit.cob raises the condition in a FUNCTION-ID whose declarative ends in EXIT FUNCTION. At 2002 it prints 'F-HANDLED=EC-FLOW-RELEASE' and 'MAIN-1 V=7' and exits 0: no abnormal end, which is correct for 2002. At 2023 it is refused COBOL0902. rel-normal.cob, with a declarative that completes normally, ends the run abnormally with exit 1 at both editions, as both texts require. rel-other-sd.cob does a RELEASE of another SD's record inside the SORT's input procedure, and the handler ends in RESUME. At both editions the SORT ends and AFTER-SORT prints, which is correct by 2002 SORT GR16 (RESUME means the USE procedure did not complete normally). The EXIT FUNCTION route belongs to the exception-processing clause's own rows, not to this sentence (same reading as q-26 and q-34 on fatal-EC rules). The compiler is correct there anyway, so this is not a false green.

cases.reason: The RESUME format is identical. I compared the 2002 and 2023 USE formats (14.8.45.1 and 14.9.49.2): GLOBAL appears in Format 1 (file exception) and Format 2 (BEFORE REPORTING) in both, and Formats 3 and 4 have no GLOBAL in either. 2002 Annex A (communications) adds no USE format, and 2002 has no USE FOR DEBUGGING.
